steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Once we clear these abandoned plates, the Exemplars will be able to reach Londinium's walls.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Ever since we broke through the pass at Silverrock Bluffs, the Nachzehrer forces have been in full retreat. And here we thought the Sarkaz would be waiting to ambush us in the ruins, but...

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: There isn't a single one in sight.

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: That strange crimson color in the sky has also started to dissipate.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: To be honest, my nerves are still a little shot. The battles in the past few days have been nightmarish.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Too many fought with their lives for this victory, pushing through all the pain and hardship...

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Anyway, this is a victory that belongs to each and every one of us.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Our home is just around the corner.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Let's pick up the pace, and—
Suddenly, a massive roar fills the air, and the entire building begins to tremble.
A strange, piercing howl comes from deep inside the building, shattering the few remaining intact windows.

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Knew it wouldn't be that easy!

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: All other teams, fall in!

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: What was that howling sound? The sound of steam?

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Vina, can it be––

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Notify the other teams and have them evacuate the building immediately. They are to stay on high alert, find cover, and be ready for anti-air operations.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Our team will proceed in a defensive formation while looking out for any potential attacks.

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Vina, when you left the Mausoleum of Kings, you all said the Steam Knight had gone mad!

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: But he helped us in the battle at Silverrock Bluffs, didn't he? Everyone's talkin' about how Victoria's glory has returned!

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Then, what's his deal now...?
Indeed, Siege can still remember the moment she was lifted by that massive armor, as well as the dull roar coming from it.
'Glorious—Victoria!'
She could not tell if the sounds from that armor were identical to the ones she had heard inside the Mausoleum of Kings. After all, the steel armor made all echoes sound similar.
Is it possible that the one inside the armor is...
Siege shakes her head, dispelling those ridiculous thoughts.
That man's courageous decision to face his own fate should not be tainted by any unrealistic fantasies.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Let's go.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: We'll have the answer when we see him.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: He should be here. At least, he was before.
The walls and the ground are scarred with traces of flames and blades, forming massive gashes that stretch deeper into the building.
It is not the first time she has seen such traces. They were also there along the corridor in front of the gate of the Mausoleum of Kings, where the statues of bygone kings stood...
According to Victorian canticles, what spews forth from the Steam Knights' blades is unyielding valor.
What about now?

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: There are Sarkaz corpses here.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: By the looks of things, this is where the Sarkaz planned to besiege and kill the last Steam Knight.
Siege recoils in horror. She has heard these words before.
A hand tugs at her sleeve.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: ...Siege.
Dagda looks at her. The two have experienced the very same thing in the Mausoleum of Kings.
The burial ground of glory.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: He is the last Steam Knight.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: If he chooses to stand in our way again like in Londinium...

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: It's alright. I know we'll have to face him sooner or later.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: ...Dagda.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: He has his duty, and we have ours.

a.text: Someone once told her that the purpose of her entire life in Londinium was merely to fulfill a duty.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Indeed...

a.text: But she has long decided not to acknowledge that anymore.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: We should cast aside all these duties and save him. Simple as that.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: Do we... have the right to do that?

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Better to act first and apologize later than to stand here worrying about it.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Let's go.
Siege ruffles the short girl's black hair and steps into the room first.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Charred corpses are everywhere, and these are pieces of the Steam Knight's armor.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: It should have been more of an encounter battle than a proper ambush. By the looks of things, the Sarkaz weren't prepared to face such a tough opponent here.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: I've taken a look around. No Sarkaz survivors.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: The only place left to search is the space deeper inside.
Behind the broken wall, the other half of the room is shrouded in thick darkness.
Not a single sound or breath can be heard from within as if the sound of steam from earlier was just an illusion.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: You all stay here and be ready to evacuate.
Siege slowly approaches the darkness deeper inside the room.
Perhaps, she would be greeted by a torrent of steam and smoke.
Perhaps, her face would soon be illuminated by the light of a blazing longsword.
Siege can't help thinking about the best outcome. Perhaps...
The friend whom she thought she had lost might be leaning next to a massive steam armor, sound asleep.

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: How are things on your side, Vina?

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Nothing here.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: The Steam Knight is already gone. The gushing and crashing sounds earlier we heard were probably the sounds of him breaking through the wall and leaving.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Maybe, he's already back in Londinium.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Let our troops outside know that the alert has been lifted. We'll continue forward in ten minutes.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: Sure. I'll make the call.
Everyone feels relieved.
Yet, Siege only sighs.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Vina, you...

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Don't worry about it.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Let's keep moving.
She does not speak a word of what she discovered.
It doesn't prove anything.
Or rather, everything has already been proven.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: The Exemplars have arrived at the designated location at the scheduled time. Londinium's walls are now within sight.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Next, we will continue northeast until we reach the outer plate. All vehicles, please confirm your coordinates...
The sunset, now no longer tainted by that vile crimson shade, forms a spectacular sight. However, Siege's mind is elsewhere.
The golden afterglow reminds her of her teacher's magnificent mane and the longsword that has been part of countless legends in her hand...
As well as––

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Vina, what are you looking at?

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Nothing in particular.
Siege clenches her fists in panic, then chuckles self-deprecatingly.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: I'm not acting like myself, am I?
She hesitates for a few seconds before opening her palm.
There, in her hand, is a tattered red cloth with burned edges.

The cloth begins to flutter in the blustery wind. Delphine hurriedly tries to grasp the cloth before the wind carries it away, but Siege loosens her grip, letting it fly away until it disappears into the distance.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: What was that?

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Something I found in that abandoned plate.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: It might've been just another piece of clothing lying around. It might've been there all along and had nothing to do with the Steam Knight.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: (Red clothing...)

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Do you think Allerdale Cumberland might still be alive?

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: There are many people whom I hope are still alive. However, such wishes are meaningless—it's like wishing I were still a street thug back in Norport, and that none of this ever happened.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: I heard from members of the Self-Salvation Corps that Allerdale Cumberland was their former leader. She never returned from the mission to retrieve the Sighs of Kings.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: She sacrificed herself for us.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: But that's not the whole story, is it?

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: You know what my old job was.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Back in Londinium, the kind of intel I was chiefly responsible for gathering, apart from the movement of the Sarkaz, was about secret agents like me.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: The Duke of Cumberland is no more, but his heir still moves freely about in Londinium. We all know what that means.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Vina, I have no intention of influencing your opinion of her, but there is no unconditional kindness and support among the Victorian worthies. I must say that––

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: She approached me with an agenda.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: I know. We... had a heart-to-heart talk. She worked for Caster, helping her to seize the Sighs of Kings.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: And despite all that, you still hope to see her alive.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: I... am still willing to see her as a friend.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: This is a dangerous decision driven by your emotions, Vina. An army can't maintain itself without discipline.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: I know, Delphine. Allerdale and I know this is an irreparable and unforgivable sin.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Still, I regret not being powerful enough to save her... and many others.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: I've never had any direct dealings with Lady Cumberland, only seeing her a few times in Londinium from a distance. She put a lot of effort into maintaining a dignified appearance.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: I can imagine the price she had to pay for that.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: I might come off as insensitive to say this, but I've met many people like Lady Cumberland. That's just the way the game is played in this country.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: She was just another actor on the stage, and her fate was not in her own hands.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: I might be able to break free from that... because I met you.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Because of all of you, I have the option to break free from the inertia of depravity and to stop playing a pitiful, supporting role at the worthies' gatherings.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: But Lady Cumberland? She was alone and helpless back then.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Allerdale... I always saw her as one who faced her fate with her head held high. She was not some loser who decided to give in.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Is that its own kind of laziness—to blame each and every tragedy on cruel fate, Delphine?

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: It's a form of laziness I've grown accustomed to.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Many things cannot be achieved through sheer hard work, Vina. We use 'fate' to describe these vast and intangible forces because they cannot be defied.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Hah. The 'inertia of depravity,' right?

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Those who step out of line will be culled—gently, yet decisively—just like the Steam Knights.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Just like... Alistair, my father.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Vina...

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Don't worry, I have no interest in raising a stink in his name. To be honest, I never even knew him that well.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Funnily enough, when I was young, my adoptive parents used to tell me stories about my father, the great 'King Alistair,' all the time...

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: But they passed away too early that I barely remember those stories anymore.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: It wasn't until Allerdale mentioned the King's name to me again that all those fragmented memories started to rush back. Rash, ambitious, determined to accomplish something big...

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Haha, I'm not sure what similarities we share beyond our blood ties. He was a monarch hanged for his failed reforms, offending nearly all the nobles.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: As for me, I'm just a Norport gangster. The only place I'm familiar with, besides the bar and boxing gym, is the police station.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: We share the surname of 'Victoria,' but that's about it.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: The Duke of Windermere's duty has always been to safeguard the border between Victoria and Leithanien. We've never paid much attention to the political struggles taking place in Londinium.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: But... it's true that my mother spoke very little of the coup and King Alistair.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: I think she deliberately avoided talking about it. I actually analyzed the situation before—

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: There wasn't anything she could do, and I understand that. Delphine, you don't need to feel sorry for me. That's just how the rules of the game are in Victoria—beneath the calm facade, everything has already been decided.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Regardless of what my mother thought at the time, I don't think the people were at fault for seeking change.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Change is something we all want, isn't it? It's just that... nobody knows how to go about it.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Yes. Everyone back then knew something was wrong, just as they do now.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: This war indeed is reshaping Victoria, but in what direction?

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: But... are we truly getting any closer to the future we hope for?

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: We've just witnessed Wellington's betrayal, as well as the indecision of the dukes. These are things that've happened time and again.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Delphine, what do you think is the reason behind everything we're facing and what our country is going through?

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Do you really want my opinion?

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Simply put, it's because we've been deceived by the brutal and cunning Sarkaz.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: All Victoria needs is time. I could easily come to the same conclusion as every noble reading newspaper in their manor.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: But we've seen it firsthand.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Our 'glorious homeland' is short-sighted, arrogant, and reckless. It is filled with greedy nobles, incompetent bureaucrats, a weak parliament, and landowners or factory owners who exploit their workers...

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: The problem is that Victoria might always has been this way, even during what people consider as her golden age.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: ––All of these things are the sources of Victoria's former glory, yet they are also the inertia that we so despise.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: But then again, we have a team now. It might be time to do more.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: What do you mean?

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Ah. It suddenly dawned on me that I might share another similarity with my father.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Both our enemy is 'Victoria.'

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: He might've been too reckless, but I might not be any better than him either. Maybe... I'll even meet the same end as he did.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: But it's still worth a shot, isn't it?

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Vina—I mean, Alexandrina Vina Victoria—do you know what you're saying right now?

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Indeed, we've found ourselves some companions, and the Exemplars have created a miracle in this battle...

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: But this is just Londinium, a single city! How many cities are there across of all Victoria?

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: The soldiers and officers involved in this war see you as a hero because the dukes—

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: The dukes need a hero to cover up their failures. We are just icons they use as a front. I'm well aware of that.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: But, so what?

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: We're already here.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Everything that has driven Victoria's 'inertia,' the obsession with glory, the worship of splendor, the monarchy, and the puppet Parliament...

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Must end here.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: You want to change all of that?

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: More than just change.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: I will wage war against them.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: It certainly won't be an easy task. We might need to fight against everything that makes up this country, including ourselves. It might take a long, long time, up to a decade or even two...

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: But if I want to make sure what happened in Londinium today never happens again, this is the only way.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: I need to vanquish the Victoria of the past until I'm the only one left in the ring.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: That's a distant dream. And, rationally speaking, it might never even come true.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: There's no shortage of reformers and even revolutionaries in this country. Some succeeded, while others failed.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Yet, all their efforts invariably ended up lost in the mists of Londinium. And Victoria has never changed.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: But... Vina, you'll treat this as a ring, won't you?

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: That's right. Regardless of what I face, there's only one thing I can do—give it a good 'slobberknocker'.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: *sigh*.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Just to be clear, I have no intent on stepping into the ring with you.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: But... if you do manage to land a few good punches, I'll be cheering for you.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Sounds good.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: It's time to let the people of Londinium know that the Exemplars are on their side!

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: We... are home.
Siege catches a glimpse of a golden figure flashing from the corner of her eyes.
Her adoptive father once told her in a hopeful tone that her teacher was the very symbol of Victoria.
With him at her side, she would lead the country until all suffering was banished by the light of glory.
What would her teacher be thinking now?
His strides are always so quick, and his appearances are always unpredictable.
His golden mane protects her from the wind and keeps her warm through the coldest nights.
He exudes an aura that resembles the sun.
But... he has not been seen for years.

steps.name: Gawain
steps.text: Vina.
The coffin was too big, and my hands felt sore. Even with the help of adults, carrying the coffin into the cemetery was a laborous task.
My adoptive father was buried right next to my adoptive mother. They both shared the same gravestone.
Those visitors who used to frequent my place when I was little didn't show up. They must have given up already. After all, it's been so long.

steps.name: Gawain
steps.text: You've gained knowledge, learned to fight, and equipped yourself with survival skills.

steps.name: Gawain
steps.text: There is nothing left for me to teach you.
My teacher seemed to let out a gentle sigh. He turned around, his golden mane coming close to my face.
As always, it smelled like sunlight.

steps.name: Gawain
steps.text: But, my child, you do not know where to go.

steps.name: Gawain
steps.text: You do not know what to do with the things you've learned from me.

a.text: 'They always said that the reason I can see you is because I have a duty.'

steps.name: Gawain
steps.text: No, there's no such thing as duty.

steps.name: Gawain
steps.text: It applies to both you and me.

steps.name: Gawain
steps.text: Only the shackled call their chains their duty.

steps.name: Gawain
steps.text: If you're finally ready to step forward...

steps.name: Gawain
steps.text: Then, I—

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: One minute, I'm getting a new message—

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Understood. Please continue the investigation, and ask Rhodes Island for help if necessary.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: What happened?

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Our technicians have detected a signal that has been listening to our conversations.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Is it the duke? Or the Sarkaz?

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Strangely enough, neither.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: According to the signal analysis... the perpetrator's name is one that I've never heard of before...

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: The people of Londinium seem to call her 'Millscar'.
